## Natural history notes

A small treefrog characterized by its smooth skin, rounded toe pads, and highly variable green, brown, or gray coloration. In Florida, it is found in many moist habitats including pine flatwoods, hammocks, swamps, marsh edges, gardens, yards, and other areas with vegetation. It is most active at night, especially after rain, and feeds on small insects and other invertebrates, with males producing a nasal, squirrel-like call during the breeding season.
